why_wrong.C: Systems Manager Run Command executes commands, doesn't specifically enable cross-account EFS mounting. Wrong tool for this requirement.

explanation.exam_tips: For cross-account EFS: amazon-efs-utils + access point + VPC connectivity (peering/TGW). Access points simplify multi-account access. VPC sharing requires redeployment. EFS mount needs network path (peering/TGW).
explanation.memorize: Cross-account EFS = amazon-efs-utils + access point + VPC connectivity

question_en: A company recently launched a new application for its customers. The application runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. End users use TCP to communicate with the application. The application must be highly available and must automatically scale as the number of users increases. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Add a Network Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
options.B: Configure an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances.
options.C: Add an Application Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.
options.D: Manually add more EC2 instances for the application.
options.E: Add a Gateway Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instances.

explanation.why_correct: Network Load Balancer handles TCP traffic efficiently at Layer 4 (transport layer). Auto Scaling group automatically adds/removes EC2 instances based on demand. Together provide high availability across two AZs with automatic scaling. Cost-effective—scale only when needed.

why_wrong.C: Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS), not optimized for generic TCP traffic. Use ALB for web protocols, NLB for TCP.
why_wrong.D: Manual scaling doesn't provide automatic response to user growth. Operational overhead, delayed capacity adjustments.
why_wrong.E: Gateway Load Balancer for deploying third-party virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS). Wrong use case—not for application load balancing.

explanation.exam_tips: For TCP traffic HA + auto-scale: NLB + Auto Scaling. ALB = HTTP/HTTPS (Layer 7), NLB = TCP/UDP (Layer 4), GLB = virtual appliances. Auto Scaling provides elasticity vs. manual capacity management.
explanation.memorize: TCP HA + auto-scale cost-effective = NLB + Auto Scaling group
explanation.architectural_concept: TCP Load Balancing with Auto Scaling

question_en: A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS. The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create AWS Cloud Formation templates for the customers.
options.B: Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
options.C: Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
options.D: Create AWS Config items for the customers.

explanation.why_correct: AWS Service Catalog provides centralized management of IT services as products. Enables self-service provisioning with governance controls. Customers deploy approved solutions from catalog without central team intervention. Maintains version control, access policies, and consistent configurations across customers.

why_wrong.A: CloudFormation templates alone lack centralized management, versioning, access control, and self-service portal that Service Catalog provides.
why_wrong.C: Systems Manager focused on operational management (patching, automation), not solution deployment and customer self-service provisioning.
why_wrong.D: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not designed for deploying and managing customer-facing solution portfolios.

explanation.exam_tips: For centralized solution management + self-service: Service Catalog (not CloudFormation alone). Service Catalog adds governance layer over CloudFormation. Don't confuse Config (compliance) with Catalog (provisioning).
explanation.memorize: Centralized solutions + self-service = AWS Service Catalog

question_en: A company is building an application in the AWS Cloud. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company uses Amazon Route 53 for the DNS. The company needs a managed solution with proactive engagement to detect against DDoS attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS Config. Configure an AWS Config managed rule that detects DDoS attacks.
options.B: Enable AWS WAF on the ALB Create an AWS WAF web ACL with rules to detect and prevent DDoS attacks. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
options.C: Store the ALB access logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to detect and take automated preventative actions for DDoS attacks.
options.D: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Configure hosted zones in Route 53 Add ALB resources as protected resources.

explanation.why_correct: AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection with 24/7 access to DDoS Response Team (DRT). Proactive engagement during attacks. Protects Route 53, ALB, CloudFront as protected resources. Financial protection against DDoS-related costs. Managed service with detailed attack diagnostics and mitigation.

why_wrong.A: AWS Config tracks configuration, doesn't detect or mitigate DDoS attacks. Wrong service for DDoS protection.
why_wrong.B: AWS WAF mitigates some application-layer attacks but doesn't provide comprehensive DDoS protection or proactive DRT engagement like Shield Advanced.
why_wrong.C: GuardDuty detects threats from logs/events, not specifically DDoS protection. Doesn't provide DDoS Response Team or proactive engagement.

explanation.exam_tips: For DDoS protection + proactive engagement: Shield Advanced (not WAF, GuardDuty, Config). Shield Standard = automatic (free), Shield Advanced = proactive + DRT. WAF = application layer rules (subset of DDoS).
explanation.memorize: DDoS + proactive engagement = Shield Advanced (DRT access, protected resources)

question_en: A company is designing a new ecommerce application for a high-traffic retail website. The application needs to process a large volume of customer orders. The application must scale to handle spikes in order volume during peak shopping events. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use a single large Amazon EC2 instance to run processing logic and to store order information. Run a relational database on the same EC2 instance.
options.B: Use a single Amazon EC2 instance to run processing logic. Control the flow of orders into the EC2 instance by using an Amazon SQS queue. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store order information.
options.C: Use an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API and an AWS Lambda function to process orders. Use Amazon DynamoDB in on-demand mode to store order information.
options.D: Use an Application Load Balancer ALB to distribute order processing traffic across multiple Amazon EC2 instances that run processing logic. Use Amazon Aurora with multiple reader nodes as the database.

explanation.why_correct: API Gateway receives HTTP API requests at scale. Lambda processes orders serverlessly—auto-scales per request. DynamoDB on-demand mode automatically scales read/write capacity for unpredictable spikes without provisioning. Completely serverless—zero infrastructure management, infinite elasticity.

why_wrong.A: Single EC2 instance with database creates single point of failure and scaling bottleneck. Can't handle spikes or high traffic.
why_wrong.B: Single EC2 with SQS buffers traffic but instance remains bottleneck. S3 inappropriate for transactional order storage (eventual consistency, no ACID).
why_wrong.D: ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling + Aurora provides scalability but requires infrastructure management. More operational overhead vs. serverless. Aurora readers don't solve write-heavy order ingestion.

explanation.exam_tips: For high-traffic spikes serverless: API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB on-demand. Don't use single instance (bottleneck) or S3 for transactional data. On-demand mode auto-scales without throttling.
explanation.memorize: High-traffic spikes serverless = API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB on-demand

question_en: A company hosts a public web application on AWS. The website has a three-tier architecture. The frontend web tier is comprised of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application tier is a second Auto Scaling group. The database tier is an Amazon RDS database. The company has configured the Auto Scaling groups to handle the application ' s normal level of demand. During an unexpected spike in demand, the company notices a long delay in the startup time when the frontend and application layers scale out. The company needs to improve the scaling performance of the application without negatively affecting the user experience. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Decrease the minimum number of EC2 instances for both Auto Scaling groups. Increase the desired number of instances to meet the peak demand requirement.
options.B: Configure the maximum number of instances for both Auto Scaling groups to be the number required to meet the peak demand. Create a warm pool.
options.C: Increase the maximum number of EC2 instances for both Auto Scaling groups to meet the normal demand requirement. Create a warm pool.
options.D: Reconfigure both Auto Scaling groups to use a scheduled scaling policy. Increase the size of the EC2 instance types and the RDS instance types.

explanation.why_correct: Warm pools maintain pre-initialized EC2 instances ready for immediate activation. Instances already booted, configured, application loaded. Dramatically reduces scale-out delay from minutes to seconds. Cost-effective—warm instances in stopped state (no compute charges). Maximum instances set to peak demand capacity.

why_wrong.A: Decreasing minimum doesn't improve startup time. Increasing desired to peak wastes money running unnecessary instances constantly.
why_wrong.C: Increasing maximum alone doesn't improve startup time—instances still start from scratch. Warm pool needed for pre-initialization.
why_wrong.D: Scheduled scaling predictive but doesn't reduce startup time. Larger instance types increase cost. RDS instance size unrelated to frontend/app tier scaling delay.

explanation.exam_tips: For reducing Auto Scaling startup time: warm pools (pre-initialized instances). Don't confuse max capacity (how many) with warm pools (how fast). Warm instances stopped = low cost. Pre-initialization key to faster scale-out.
explanation.memorize: Fast scale-out + cost-effective = Auto Scaling warm pools (pre-initialized)

question_en: A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to AWS. The database consists of a single table that contains millions of geographic information systems (GIS) images that are high resolution and are identified by a geographic code. When a natural disaster occurs, tens of thousands of images get updated every few minutes. Each geographic code has a single image or row that is associated with it. The company wants a solution that is highly available and scalable during such events.

options.A: Store the images and geographic codes in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
options.B: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Use Amazon DynamoDB with the geographic code as the key and the image S3 URL as the value.
options.C: Store the images and geographic codes in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) during times of high load.
options.D: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Store geographic codes and image S3 URLs in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.

explanation.why_correct: S3 almacena imágenes grandes eficientemente a escala masiva, DynamoDB provee baja latencia con el código geográfico como partition key, auto-escala para manejar picos durante desastres naturales, y separa metadata de binarios. Esta arquitectura es serverless, altamente disponible y cost-effective según AWS best practices.

why_wrong.A: RDS no está diseñado para almacenar millones de imágenes binarias grandes. Alto costo, pobre escalabilidad y límites de almacenamiento lo hacen inadecuado.
why_wrong.C: DynamoDB tiene límite de 400 KB por item, imposible almacenar imágenes de alta resolución directamente. Viola best practices de diseño.
why_wrong.D: Mismos problemas que A: RDS no es apropiado para almacenar imágenes binarias a gran escala, independiente de dónde estén las referencias.

explanation.exam_tips: Patrón común SAA-C03: imágenes/videos en S3, metadata en DynamoDB. Reconoce cuando separar datos grandes (S3) de referencias (NoSQL). DynamoDB brilla con claves simples y alto throughput.
explanation.memorize: Binarios grandes → S3. Referencias/metadata → DynamoDB con S3 URL.

question_en: A software company needs to upgrade a critical web application. The application is hosted in a public subnet. The EC2 instance runs a MySQL database. The application ' s DNS records are published in an Amazon Route 53 zone. A solutions architect must reconfigure the application to be scalable and highly available. The solutions architect must also reduce MySQL read latency. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Launch a second EC2 instance in a second AWS Region. Use a Route 53 failover routing policy to redirect the traffic to the second EC2 instance.
options.B: Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
options.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. Create the primary DB instance and reader DB instance in separate Availability Zones.
options.D: Create and configure an Auto Scaling group to launch private EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Add the instances to a target group behind a new Application Load Balancer.
options.E: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with cross-Region read replicas.

explanation.why_correct: Auto Scaling group con instancias en múltiples AZs detrás de ALB provee escalabilidad horizontal y alta disponibilidad. Aurora MySQL con reader endpoints en diferentes AZs distribuye lecturas, reduce latencia de reads y ofrece failover automático. Combinación cumple escalabilidad, disponibilidad y performance.

why_wrong.A: Multi-Region incrementa costo y complejidad sin ser necesario. Failover entre regiones es más lento que multi-AZ.
why_wrong.D: Auto Scaling no funciona cross-Region de esta manera. ALB no puede distribuir tráfico entre regiones directamente.
why_wrong.E: Cross-Region read replicas son excesivos para este caso. Multi-AZ cumple el requisito de read latency sin complejidad adicional.

explanation.exam_tips: Multi-select: busca combos que resuelvan diferentes aspectos (compute + database). ALB + Auto Scaling + Aurora Multi-AZ es patrón gold standard para aplicaciones web escalables.
explanation.memorize: Escalabilidad + disponibilidad = Auto Scaling multi-AZ + Aurora reader endpoints.

question_en: A company runs a web application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. A company employee caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table. The company must be able to recover from similar incidents in the future. The company must be able to restore the database to a specific point in time within the previous 30 days. The solution must restore the database with a maximum of 5 minutes of data loss. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Read replicas
options.B: Manual snapshots
options.C: Automated backups
options.D: Multi-AZ deployments

explanation.why_correct: Automated backups en RDS combinan daily snapshots con transaction logs subidos cada 5 minutos, permitiendo point-in-time recovery (PITR) hasta 35 días atrás. Cumple exactamente requisito: restaurar a punto específico dentro de 30 días con máximo 5 minutos de pérdida.

why_wrong.A: Read replicas replican datos para escalabilidad de lectura, no permiten restaurar a punto en el tiempo anterior. No ayudan con errores humanos.
why_wrong.B: Manual snapshots son capturas específicas, no proveen recuperación continua point-in-time entre snapshots. Requieren intervención manual.
why_wrong.D: Multi-AZ provee alta disponibilidad contra fallas de infraestructura, no protege contra errores humanos o corrupción de datos.

explanation.exam_tips: Automated backups = PITR. Manual snapshots = backup específico sin granularidad temporal. Multi-AZ ≠ backup. Read replicas ≠ recovery histórico. Busca palabras 'specific point in time' o 'accidental deletion'.
explanation.memorize: PITR con ≤5 min pérdida = RDS automated backups con transaction logs.

question_en: A company runs a non-production application on an Amazon EC2 instance that has the Amazon CloudWatch agent installed. The CloudWatch agent monitors application processes and sends custom metrics to CloudWatch. The application has a critical bug that causes crashes that require an instance reboot. The company does not currently have the resources to address the bug, but the server needs to remain as operational as possible. The company manually reboots the instance several times each day. The company needs a solution to automate the instance reboots until the company can address the root cause of the bug. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Use a CloudWatch alarm state change event to invoke Amazon EventBridge to run AWS Systems Manager Run Command to restart the instance.
options.B: Use a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run AWS Systems Manager Run Command to restart the instance.
options.C: Use a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon SNS topic that notifies the operations team to restart the instance.
options.D: Use a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function that automatically notifies the company through chat to restart the instance.

explanation.why_correct: CloudWatch alarm state changes se publican automáticamente a EventBridge. EventBridge puede invocar Systems Manager Run Command para reiniciar instancias EC2 remotamente. Esta solución es completamente serverless, sin código custom Lambda, mínima overhead operacional y usa servicios nativos AWS.

why_wrong.B: Funcional pero agrega Lambda innecesario. Menos eficiente que integración directa EventBridge → SSM Run Command. Más overhead operacional.
why_wrong.C: Missing key requirement: optimal service selection.
why_wrong.D: Similar a C: notificación vía chat requiere acción manual. No automatiza el reinicio.

explanation.exam_tips: 'Least operational overhead' con automatización = servicios nativos integrados sin custom code. CloudWatch → EventBridge → SSM es patrón común. Lambda agrega overhead a menos que se requiera lógica custom.
explanation.memorize: CloudWatch alarm → EventBridge → SSM Run Command = reinicio automático sin Lambda.

question_en: A global ecommerce company runs its critical workloads on AWS. The workloads use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance that is configured for a Multi-AZ deployment. Customers have reported application timeouts when the company undergoes database failovers. The company needs a resilient solution to reduce failover time Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon RDS Proxy. Assign the proxy to the DB instance.
options.B: Create a read replica for the DB instance Move the read traffic to the read replica.
options.C: Enable Performance Insights. Monitor the CPU load to identify the timeouts.
options.D: Take regular automatic snapshots Copy the automatic snapshots to multiple AWS Regions

explanation.why_correct: RDS Proxy mantiene connection pool y maneja failovers transparentemente para la aplicación. Reduce failover time al mantener conexiones activas y redirigir automáticamente durante failover Multi-AZ. Minimiza timeouts sin cambios en código de aplicación. Fully managed y altamente disponible.

why_wrong.B: Read replicas mejoran performance de lectura pero no reducen failover time del primary database durante failover Multi-AZ.
why_wrong.C: Performance Insights es herramienta de monitoreo/diagnóstico, no reduce failover time ni resuelve timeouts.
why_wrong.D: Snapshots son para backup/recovery, no mejoran resiliencia durante failovers en tiempo real.

explanation.exam_tips: Cuando veas 'application timeouts during failovers' piensa RDS Proxy. Es el servicio diseñado específicamente para este problema. Connection pooling + automatic failover handling.
explanation.memorize: Timeouts en failovers RDS = RDS Proxy con connection pooling.

question_en: A solutions architect has an application container, an AWS Lambda function, and an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The Lambda function uses the SQS queue as an event source. The Lambda function makes a call to a third-party machine learning (ML) API when the function is invoked. The response from the third-party API can take up to 60 seconds to return. The Lambda function ' s timeout value is currently 65 seconds. The solutions architect has noticed that the Lambda function sometimes processes duplicate messages from the SQS queue. What should the solutions architect do to ensure that the Lambda function does not process duplicate messages?

options.A: Configure the Lambda function with a larger amount of memory.
options.B: Configure an increase in the Lambda function ' s timeout value.
options.C: Configure the SQS queue ' s delivery delay value to be greater than the maximum time it takes to call the third-party API.
options.D: Configure the SQS queue ' s visibility timeout value to be greater than the maximum time it takes to call the third-party API.

explanation.why_correct: SQS visibility timeout oculta mensaje durante procesamiento. Si Lambda tarda 60s procesando pero visibility timeout es menor, mensaje reaparece en queue y se procesa duplicate. Configurar visibility timeout > max execution time (65s+) previene que mensaje se haga visible antes de completar procesamiento.

why_wrong.A: Memoria de Lambda no afecta manejo de mensajes duplicados en SQS. No resuelve el problema raíz.
why_wrong.B: Timeout de 65s ya es suficiente (60s API + overhead). Incrementarlo no soluciona visibility timeout inadecuado.
why_wrong.C: Delivery delay controla cuándo mensaje está disponible inicialmente, no previene reprocesamiento después de comenzar procesamiento.

explanation.exam_tips: Lambda + SQS: visibility timeout debe ser > Lambda timeout. Patrón común examen: mensajes duplicados = visibility timeout muy bajo. Delivery delay ≠ visibility timeout.
explanation.memorize: SQS visibility timeout debe exceder Lambda max execution time para evitar duplicados.

question_en: A company has an application that runs only on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with scheduled scaling actions. However, the capacity does not always increase at the scheduled times, and instances terminate many times a day. A solutions architect must ensure that the instances launch on time and have fewer interruptions. Which action will meet these requirements?

options.A: Specify the capacity-optimized allocation strategy for Spot Instances. Add more instance types to the Auto Scaling group.
options.B: B. Specify the capacity-optimized allocation strategy for Spot Instances. Increase the size of the instances in the Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Specify the lowest-price allocation strategy for Spot Instances. Add more instance types to the Auto Scaling group.
options.D: Specify the lowest-price allocation strategy for Spot Instances. Increase the size of the instances in the Auto Scaling group.

explanation.why_correct: Capacity-optimized allocation strategy selecciona Spot pools con mayor capacidad disponible, reduciendo interrupciones significativamente vs lowest-price. Agregar múltiples instance types amplía pools disponibles, incrementando probabilidad de encontrar capacidad. Combinación optimiza disponibilidad de Spot Instances para scheduled scaling.

why_wrong.B: Aumentar tamaño de instancias no incrementa availability de Spot capacity. Limita opciones de pools disponibles.
why_wrong.C: Lowest-price prioriza costo sobre disponibilidad, resulta en más interrupciones cuando AWS necesita capacidad. Opuesto al objetivo.
why_wrong.D: Combina dos errores: lowest-price (más interrupciones) y solo un instance type (menos pools).

explanation.exam_tips: Spot Instances: capacity-optimized > lowest-price para reducir interrupciones. Instance type diversity = más pools = mejor availability. Scheduled scaling + Spot requiere estrategia de capacidad sólida.
explanation.memorize: Menos interrupciones Spot = capacity-optimized + múltiples instance types.

question_en: A company is building a critical data processing application that will run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company must not run any two nodes on the same underlying hardware. The company requires at least 99.99% availability for the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the application to one Availability Zone by using a cluster placement group strategy.
options.B: Deploy the application to three Availability Zones by using a spread placement group strategy.
options.C: Deploy the application to three Availability Zones by using a cluster placement group strategy.
options.D: Deploy the application to one Availability Zone by using a partition placement group strategy.

explanation.why_correct: Spread placement group garantiza que cada instancia se coloque en hardware físico diferente. Distribuir en tres AZs provee fault isolation contra fallas de AZ completo. Combinación cumple requisito de no compartir hardware y alcanza 99.99% availability mediante redundancia multi-AZ.

why_wrong.A: Cluster placement group coloca instancias cerca para baja latencia pero en mismo hardware. Viola requisito y un solo AZ no cumple 99.99%.
why_wrong.C: Cluster placement no separa hardware físico. Multi-AZ no compensa esta deficiencia para el requisito específico.
why_wrong.D: Partition placement separa partitions pero instancias dentro de partition pueden compartir hardware. Un solo AZ insuficiente para 99.99%.

explanation.exam_tips: Spread = máxima separación de hardware (7 instancias/AZ máximo). Cluster = baja latencia, mismo rack. Partition = separación de grupos grandes. 99.99% requiere multi-AZ siempre.
explanation.memorize: Hardware separado + 99.99% availability = spread placement multi-AZ.

question_en: A solutions architect is designing a multi-Region disaster recovery (DR) strategy for a company. The company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups that are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company hosts the application in the company ' s primary and secondary AWS Regions. The application must respond to DNS queries from the secondary Region if the primary Region fails. Only one Region must serve traffic at a time. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an outbound endpoint in Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Create forwarding rules that determine how queries will be forwarded to DNS resolvers on the network. Associate the rules with VPCs in each Region.
options.B: Create primary and secondary DNS records in Amazon Route 53. Configure health checks and a failover routing policy.
options.C: Create a traffic policy in Amazon Route 53. Use a geolocation routing policy and a value type of ELB Application Load Balancer.
options.D: Create an Amazon Route 53 profile. Associate DNS resources to the profile. Associate the profile with VPCs in each Region.

explanation.why_correct: Route 53 failover routing policy con health checks monitorea primary endpoint. Si falla health check, automáticamente redirige DNS queries a secondary Region. Asegura solo una Region activa (active-passive) y failover automático sin intervención manual. Diseño estándar para DR multi-Region.

why_wrong.A: Outbound endpoints y forwarding rules son para resolución DNS híbrida on-prem, no para DR multi-Region de aplicaciones.
why_wrong.C: Geolocation routing distribuye tráfico por ubicación geográfica del usuario, no provee failover automático basado en salud del endpoint.
why_wrong.D: Route 53 profiles son para compartir configuraciones DNS entre VPCs, no para failover multi-Region.

explanation.exam_tips: DR multi-Region active-passive = Route 53 failover policy + health checks. Geolocation es para distribución geográfica, no DR. Busca palabras 'only one Region serving traffic'.
explanation.memorize: DR active-passive multi-Region = Route 53 failover policy con health checks.

question_en: A company recently launched a new product that is highly available in one AWS Region The product consists of an application that runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), apublic Application Load Balancer (ALB), and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants a solution that will make the application highly available across Regions. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select THREE.)

options.A: In a different Region, deploy the application to a new ECS cluster that is accessible through a new ALB.
options.B: Create an Amazon Route 53 failover record.
options.C: Modify the DynamoDB table to create a DynamoDB global table.
options.D: In the same Region, deploy the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that is accessible through a new ALB.
options.E: Modify the DynamoDB table to create global secondary indexes (GSIs).
options.F: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint for the application.

explanation.why_correct: Desplegar ECS + ALB en Region diferente provee redundancia de compute. Route 53 failover dirige tráfico a Region sana automáticamente. DynamoDB Global Tables replica datos bidireccionalmente entre Regions con latencia sub-segundo. Las tres juntas logran multi-Region high availability completa.

why_wrong.D: Does not provide sufficient redundancy or failover capability to meet availability requirements.
why_wrong.E: GSIs mejoran queries dentro de una tabla pero no replican datos cross-Region. No proveen disponibilidad multi-Region.
why_wrong.F: PrivateLink es para conectividad privada entre VPCs/servicios, no para alta disponibilidad multi-Region.

explanation.exam_tips: Multi-Region HA requiere: compute en ambas Regions (A), DNS inteligente (B), datos replicados (C). DynamoDB Global Tables ≠ GSIs. Multi-select: identifica componentes complementarios no redundantes.
explanation.memorize: Multi-Region HA = compute duplicado + Route 53 failover + Global Tables.

question_en: A company is building a serverless application to process clickstream data from its website. The clickstream data is sent to an Amazon Kinesis Data Streams data stream from the application web servers. The company wants to enrich the clickstream data by joining the clickstream data with customer profile data from an Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ database. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift to analyze the enriched data. The solution must be highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to process and enrich the clickstream data. Use the same Lambda function to write the clickstream data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the enriched data in Amazon S3.
options.B: Use an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance to poll the data stream and enrich the clickstream data. Configure the EC2 instance to use the COPY command to send the enriched results to Amazon Redshift.
options.C: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task with AWS Fargate Spot capacity to poll the data stream and enrich the clickstream data. Configure an Amazon EC2 instance to use the COPY command to send the enriched results to Amazon Redshift.
options.D: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to load the clickstream data from Kinesis Data Streams to Amazon S3. Use AWS Glue crawlers to infer the schema and populate the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Use Amazon Athena to query the raw data in Amazon S3.

explanation.why_correct: Lambda serverless procesa streams de Kinesis con auto-scaling, enriquece con queries a Aurora, escribe a S3. Redshift Spectrum consulta datos en S3 sin cargarlos a Redshift, reduciendo costos. Lambda + Aurora Multi-AZ + S3 + Spectrum son todos highly available según AWS architecture best practices.

why_wrong.B: EC2 Spot puede ser interrumpido sin aviso, compromete alta disponibilidad. No serverless ni auto-scaling como Lambda.
why_wrong.C: ECS Fargate Spot correcto pero EC2 para COPY command agrega complejidad y punto de falla. Menos disponible que solución fully serverless.
why_wrong.D: Overly complex architecture with unnecessary service integration. Additional components increase cost, latency, and operational complexity without proportional benefit.

explanation.exam_tips: Serverless + highly available = Lambda + managed services. Spot Instances contradicen HA. Redshift Spectrum permite analytics sin ETL. Enrichment = join de múltiples fuentes, no solo query raw data.
explanation.memorize: Enriquecer streaming data serverless HA = Lambda + Aurora + S3 + Redshift Spectrum.
explanation.architectural_concept: Serverless Stream Processing with Data Enrichment

question_en: A company has an ecommerce application that users access through multiple mobile apps and web applications. The company needs a solution that will receive requests from the mobile apps and web applications through an API. Request traffic volume varies significantly throughout each day. Traffic spikes during sales events. The solution must be loosely coupled and ensure that no requests are lost. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Application Load Balancer ALB. Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk endpoint to process the requests. Add the Elastic Beanstalk endpoint to the target group of the ALB.
options.B: Set up an Amazon API Gateway REST API with an integration to an Amazon SQS queue. Configure a dead-letter queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to poll the queue to process the requests.
options.C: Create an Application Load Balancer ALB. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the requests. Add the Lambda function as a target of the ALB.
options.D: Set up an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with an integration to an Amazon SNS topic. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the requests. Subscribe the function to the SNS topic to process the requests.

explanation.why_correct: API Gateway recibe requests de mobile/web apps con auto-scaling automático. Integración directa con SQS persiste cada request durablemente en queue. Lambda polls SQS para procesar asíncronamente. DLQ captura mensajes fallidos evitando pérdida. Arquitectura loose-coupled, durable y resiliente a spikes.

why_wrong.A: ALB + Elastic Beanstalk procesa síncronamente. Si backend se sobrecarga durante spike, requests pueden perderse o timeout. No provee buffering durable.
why_wrong.C: Lambda como target de ALB procesa síncronamente sin queue buffering. Requests pueden perderse si Lambda throttling o errores durante spikes.
why_wrong.D: SNS es pub-sub para broadcast, no garantiza delivery single consumer como SQS. Menos apropiado para work queue pattern.

explanation.exam_tips: 'No requests lost' + traffic spikes = queue (SQS) entre API y procesamiento. SNS es broadcast, SQS es work queue. DLQ captura fallos. API Gateway integra nativamente con SQS sin Lambda intermedio.
explanation.memorize: Loosely coupled sin pérdida de requests = API Gateway → SQS + DLQ → Lambda.
explanation.architectural_concept: Asynchronous Request Processing with Durable Queuing

question_en: A company hosts a single-page application in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has replicated the application to a second S3 bucket in a separate AWS Region. The company has users in Asia and Europe. A solutions architect must design a solution that redirects each user ' s requests to the Region that is closest to the user. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function in one Region. Configure the function to redirect traffic to the closest Region based on the user ' s IP address. Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke the function.
options.B: Create an Application Load Balancer ALB to distribute and redirect requests to the S3 bucket that is in the closest Region based on the user ' s geolocation.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the two S3 buckets as origins. Configure CloudFront behaviors to direct user requests to the closest Region based on user geolocation.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the two S3 buckets as origins. Create an AWS Lambda@Edge function to set a specific header that indicates each user ' s location. Create behaviors for each S3 bucket origin to select the origin based on the added header.

explanation.why_correct: Lambda@Edge ejecuta en CloudFront edge locations, puede inspeccionar viewer-country header y modificar request para seleccionar origin S3 bucket más cercano. CloudFront behaviors basados en headers custom permiten routing dinámico a Region apropiada. Solución nativa CloudFront sin servicios adicionales.

why_wrong.A: Lambda en una Region no procesa requests desde edge. S3 Event Notifications se disparan por cambios en S3, no por user requests.
why_wrong.B: ALB no puede distribuir requests a S3 buckets. ALB es para compute targets (EC2, Lambda, IP), no object storage.
why_wrong.C: CloudFront behaviors estándar no soportan geolocation routing para origin selection directamente sin Lambda@Edge customization.

explanation.exam_tips: CloudFront + múltiples origins + routing dinámico = Lambda@Edge. Geolocation en CloudFront behaviors solo no es suficiente para origin selection. ALB no trabaja con S3 como target.
explanation.memorize: S3 multi-Region routing geográfico = CloudFront + Lambda@Edge con header inspection.

question_en: A company needs a solution to back up and protect critical AWS resources. The company needs to regularly take backups of several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases. To ensure high resiliency, the company must have the ability to validate and restore backups. Which solution meets the requirement with LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Backup to create a backup schedule for the resources. Use AWS Backup to create a restoration testing plan for the required resources.
options.B: Take snapshots of the EC2 instances and RDS DB instances. Create AWS Batch jobs to validate and restore the snapshots.
options.C: Create a custom AWS Lambda function to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and RDS DB instances. Create a second Lambda function to restore the snapshots periodically to validate the backups.
options.D: Take snapshots of the EC2 instances and RDS DB instances. Create an AWS Lambda function to restore the snapshots periodically to validate the backups.

explanation.why_correct: AWS Backup centraliza backup management para EC2 y RDS con backup plans automatizados. Incluye restore testing plans que validan backups automáticamente sin scripts custom. Fully managed, mínima overhead operacional, cumple best practices de resiliency y automation según Well-Architected Framework.

why_wrong.B: Snapshots manuales + AWS Batch requiere crear, mantener y debuggear custom logic. Alto overhead operacional vs servicio managed.
why_wrong.C: Dos Lambda functions custom requieren código, monitoreo, error handling y mantenimiento. Significativamente más overhead que servicio managed.
why_wrong.D: Lambda custom para validación periódica aún requiere código custom y orchestration. Más overhead que restore testing plans integrados.

explanation.exam_tips: 'Least operational overhead' para backups AWS = AWS Backup service. Siempre prefiere managed service sobre custom Lambda/scripts cuando existe. Restore testing es feature clave de AWS Backup.
explanation.memorize: Backups automatizados con validación mínima overhead = AWS Backup con restore testing plans.

question_en: A company runs a NetApp storage array in an on-premises data center. The company wants to migrate the storage array to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. The company has a mix of NFS and SMB file shares with complex directory structures and over 60 million small files. The company has 10 Gbps of network bandwidth available. The company wants to optimize migration efficiency for the file system.

options.A: Use AWS DataSync with a bandwidth throttle. Use the All tiering policy.
options.B: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Configure a zero-ETL integration with the FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system.
options.C: Set up NetApp SnapMirror replication between the on-premises array and the FSx for ONTAP file system.
options.D: Use AWS Snowball Edge to perform an offline migration.

explanation.why_correct: NetApp SnapMirror es replicación nativa block-level entre NetApp systems on-prem y FSx for ONTAP. Optimizado para transferir millones de archivos pequeños eficientemente. Preserva estructuras de directorios complejas, permisos NFS/SMB y metadata. Incremental syncs minimizan cutover time y usa 10 Gbps network completamente.

why_wrong.A: DataSync funciona pero menos eficiente que SnapMirror para datasets masivos con millones de archivos pequeños. SnapMirror es block-level vs file-level.
why_wrong.B: Storage Gateway Volume Gateway es para volúmenes block-based y acceso híbrido, no para migración completa de file shares NFS/SMB.
why_wrong.D: Snowball Edge es offline y lento (shipping delays). Con 10 Gbps disponible, SnapMirror online es más eficiente y permite syncs incrementales pre-cutover.

explanation.exam_tips: NetApp on-prem → FSx for ONTAP = SnapMirror siempre. Es la opción nativa y más eficiente. DataSync es alternativa pero SnapMirror gana para NetApp workflows. Reconoce cuando existe solución nativa vendor-specific.
explanation.memorize: Migración NetApp a FSx ONTAP optimizada = SnapMirror replication.

question_en: A company needs to design a resilient web application to process customer orders. The web application must automatically handle increases in web traffic and application usage without affecting the customer experience or losing customer orders. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use a NAT gateway to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive, process, and store processed customer orders. Use an AWS Lambda function to capture and store unprocessed orders.
options.B: Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to manage web traffic. Use an Application Load Balancer to receive customer orders from the NLB. Use Amazon Redshift with a Multi-AZ deployment to store unprocessed and processed customer orders.
options.C: Use a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to manage web traffic. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to receive and process customer orders. Use the GWLB to capture and store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store processed customer orders.
options.D: Use an Application Load Balancer to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive and process customer orders. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store processed customer orders.

explanation.why_correct: ALB distribuye tráfico web Layer 7 con health checks. Auto Scaling escala EC2 horizontalmente según demanda. SQS bufferiza orders como queue durably, previene pérdida durante spikes. RDS Multi-AZ provee database HA con failover automático. Arquitectura decoupled, resilient y scalable cumple todos requisitos.

why_wrong.A: NAT gateway es para outbound traffic de private subnets, no maneja incoming web traffic ni provee load balancing.
why_wrong.B: NLB a ALB es redundante e incorrecto. Redshift es data warehouse analítico, inapropiado para transaccional order processing.
why_wrong.C: GWLB es para network appliances (firewalls, IDS), no application traffic management. GWLB no captura/almacena orders transaccionales.

explanation.exam_tips: Order processing resiliente = ALB + Auto Scaling + SQS + RDS Multi-AZ. SQS previene pérdida de orders. NAT gateway/GWLB son distractores comunes, no manejan web traffic. Redshift ≠ transactional database.
explanation.memorize: Web app resiliente sin pérdida de datos = ALB + ASG + SQS + RDS Multi-AZ.
explanation.architectural_concept: Resilient Web Application with Message Buffering

question_en: A company uses server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys SSE-KMS to encrypt objects that the company stores in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company requires all objects in the S3 bucket to be replicated to a secondary AWS account in the same AWS Region. All objects in the source account S3 bucket must be available in the secondary account within several minutes. All replicated objects must be immediately accessible. The company has already modified the key policy for the KMS key that encrypts the bucket in the source account to allow access from the secondary account. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a new S3 bucket in the secondary account. Configure an AWS PrivateLink connection between the new S3 bucket and the existing S3 bucket. Grant PrivateLink permission to access the KMS keys that encrypt the data.
options.B: Create an AWS Backup job for the source S3 bucket. Create a backup vault in the secondary AWS account. Configure the backup plan to copy the backup jobs to the new backup vault.
options.C: Create a new S3 bucket in the secondary account. Configure an S3 replication rule on the source bucket to replicate objects to the secondary account. Enable S3 Replication Time Control S3 RTC.
options.D: Configure an AWS Lambda function in the source account to automatically invoke an Amazon S3 Batch Operations job to copy the objects to the secondary account S3 bucket every five minutes.

explanation.why_correct: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replica objetos automáticamente a bucket destino, soporta SSE-KMS con configuración apropiada de permisos. S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) garantiza 99.9% de objetos replicados en 15 minutos, cumple requisito 'within several minutes'. Objetos inmediatamente accesibles en destino.

why_wrong.A: PrivateLink no replica objetos S3 ni provee mecanismo de replicación. PrivateLink es para conectividad privada entre servicios.
why_wrong.B: AWS Backup copia snapshots pero no provee replicación near-real-time continua para nuevos objetos. Mayor latencia que S3 RTC.
why_wrong.D: Batch Operations cada 5 minutos con Lambda es solución custom compleja. Más overhead operacional que S3 native replication. Menos reliable para objetos nuevos.

explanation.exam_tips: S3 cross-account replication con KMS: CRR + S3 RTC. RTC garantiza replicación en minutos (SLA). Siempre prefiere replicación nativa S3 sobre soluciones custom Lambda/Batch Ops para este caso.
explanation.memorize: S3 replication cross-account rápida = CRR + S3 RTC con KMS key grants.

question_en: A company uses Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in its primary AWS Region for CIFS and NFS file shares. Applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances access the file shares. The company needs a storage disaster recovery (DR) solution in a secondary Region. The data that is replicated in the secondary Region needs to be accessed by using the same protocols as the primary Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Replicate the S3 bucket to the secondary Region.
options.B: Create a backup of the FSx for ONTAP volumes by using AWS Backup. Copy the volumes to the secondary Region. Create a new FSx for ONTAP instance from the backup.
options.C: Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region. Use NetApp SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary Region to the secondary Region.
options.D: Create an Amazon EFS volume. Migrate the current data to the volume. Replicate the volume to the secondary Region.

explanation.why_correct: FSx for ONTAP en secondary Region con SnapMirror replica datos eficientemente preservando todas características ONTAP. Mantiene compatibilidad CIFS y NFS protocol-level. EC2 instances pueden acceder file shares en DR Region usando mismos protocols sin cambios. Least overhead porque usa capacidades nativas ONTAP integradas.

why_wrong.A: S3 no provee file shares CIFS/NFS nativos. Cambio de platform requiere modificar acceso de aplicaciones.
why_wrong.B: Backups AWS Backup funciona pero restore manual no es solución DR activa. No provee file shares accesibles continuamente en secondary Region con mismos protocols.
why_wrong.D: EFS no soporta CIFS/SMB como FSx ONTAP. Migrar a EFS requiere cambio de platform y no preserva protocol compatibility.

explanation.exam_tips: FSx ONTAP DR = SnapMirror a segunda instancia FSx ONTAP. Preserva protocols nativos (CIFS/NFS). EFS no es equivalente SMB. S3 no provee file shares. SnapMirror es answer obvia cuando source y target son ONTAP.
explanation.memorize: DR FSx ONTAP con mismo protocol access = SnapMirror a FSx ONTAP en DR Region.
explanation.architectural_concept: File System Disaster Recovery with Protocol Preservation

question_en: A retail company is building an order fulfillment system using a microservices architecture on AWS. The system must store incoming orders durably until processing completes successfully. Multiple teams’ services process orders according to a defined workflow. Services must be scalable, loosely coupled, and able to handle sudden surges in order volume. The processing steps of each order must be centrally tracked. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Send incoming orders to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Start an AWS Step Functions workflow for each order that orchestrates the microservices. Use AWS Lambda functions for each microservice.
options.B: Send incoming orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Start an AWS Step Functions workflow for each order that orchestrates the microservices. Use AWS Lambda functions for each microservice.
options.C: Send incoming orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EventBridge to distribute events among the microservices. Use AWS Lambda functions for each microservice.
options.D: Send incoming orders to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon EventBridge to the topic to distribute events among the microservices. Use AWS Lambda functions for each microservice.

explanation.why_correct: SQS provee durable storage de orders con queue persistence. Step Functions orquesta workflow de microservices con state tracking visual y centralizado. Lambda escala automáticamente para handle surges. SQS decoupling + Step Functions orchestration + Lambda scalability cumple todos requisitos: durabilidad, tracking, loose coupling, escalabilidad.

why_wrong.A: SNS es pub-sub broadcast, no provee durable queuing 'until processing completes'. Si subscriber falla, mensaje puede perderse sin retry.
why_wrong.C: EventBridge distribuye eventos pero no provee workflow orchestration centralizado ni state tracking como Step Functions.
why_wrong.D: Combina dos debilidades: SNS (no durable queueing) y EventBridge (no workflow orchestration/tracking centralizado).

explanation.exam_tips: Durable storage + workflow tracking = SQS + Step Functions. SNS pierde mensajes si consumer falla. EventBridge es event routing, Step Functions es workflow orchestration. Busca 'centrally tracked' → Step Functions.
explanation.memorize: Microservices con workflow tracking y durabilidad = SQS + Step Functions + Lambda.

question_en: A company has a website that handles dynamic traffic loads. The website architecture is based on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that is configured to use scheduled scaling. Each EC2 instance runs code from an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume and stores shared data back to the same volume. The company wants to optimize costs for the website. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Reconfigure the Auto Scaling group to set a desired number of instances. Turn off scheduled scaling.
options.B: Create a new launch template version for the Auto Scaling group that uses larger EC2 instances.
options.C: Reconfigure the Auto Scaling group to use a target tracking scaling policy.
options.D: Replace the EFS volume with instance store volumes.

explanation.why_correct: Target tracking scaling policy ajusta capacidad automáticamente basado en métricas reales (CPU, requests, custom metrics), optimizando costo al escalar según demanda actual. Más eficiente que scheduled scaling que no adapta a cambios inesperados. Mantiene performance mientras minimiza instancias idle.

why_wrong.A: Desired number fijo no adapta a dynamic traffic loads. Sobre-provisiona o sub-provisiona constantemente, incrementando costos o afectando performance.
why_wrong.B: Instancias más grandes incrementan costo por hora significativamente. No mejora adaptación a traffic patterns dinámicos.
why_wrong.D: Instance store volumes no son persistent y datos compartidos en EFS se perderían. Viola arquitectura existente sin beneficio de costo.

explanation.exam_tips: Dynamic traffic + optimizar costos = target tracking scaling. Scheduled scaling es para patterns predecibles. Target tracking adapta continuamente. Larger instances casi nunca es answer para cost optimization.
explanation.memorize: Dynamic traffic cost optimization = target tracking scaling policy.
explanation.architectural_concept: Dynamic Auto Scaling for Cost Optimization

The application uses Amazon RDS for the database, Amazon S3 for object storage, and S3 Event Notifications that invoke AWS Lambda for serverless processing. The company uses AWS IAM Identity Center to manage user credentials. The development, testing, and operations teams need secure access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3 while ensuring the confidentiality of sensitive customer data. The solution must comply with the principle of least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use IAM roles with least privilege to grant all the teams access. Assign IAM roles to each team with customized IAM policies defining specific permission for Amazon RDS and S3 object access based on team responsibilities.
options.B: Enable IAM Identity Center with an Identity Center directory. Create and configure permission sets with granular access to Amazon RDS and Amazon S3. Assign all the teams to groups that have specific access with the permission sets.
options.C: Create individual IAM users for each member in all the teams with role-based permissions. Assign the IAM roles with predefined policies for RDS and S3 access to each user based on user needs. Implement IAM Access Analyzer for periodic credential evaluation.
options.D: Use AWS Organizations to create separate accounts for each team. Implement cross-account IAM roles with least privilege. Grant specific permission for RDS and S3 access based on team roles and responsibilities.

explanation.why_correct: This solution implements security best practices: IAM roles/policies enforce least privilege access. Reduces operational overhead:

why_wrong.A: Overly complex architecture with unnecessary service integration. Additional components increase cost, latency, and operational complexity without proportional benefit.
